answer: On an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, limiting influence from distant or weakly connected identities. If Sybil identities cluster around a meadow, wharf, or prism, their sparse external edge cut yields low conductance: few walks escape the cluster. Under a fixed walk budget and bounded edge weights, this bottleneck limits the cluster’s stationary flow from honest nodes, mathematically bounding its aggregate voting weight rather than merely counting its identities.
